site.tagline: A free, open library for reading public-domain Christian classics side by side in the original language and in Korean translation. The translations are released under CC0, so anyone may use them without conditions.

ecumenical.name: The Ancient Church
ecumenical.desc: The ecumenical creeds left by the councils of Nicaea, Constantinople, and Chalcedon and by the Western church. These are not the work of a single author but documents the church has confessed together.

calvin.name: John Calvin
calvin.desc: Reformer of Geneva. He left sermons, commentaries, the Institutes of the Christian Religion, treatises, and letters; his collected works (CO) were published in 59 volumes in 1863–1900.

beza.name: Theodore Beza
beza.desc: Calvin's successor in Geneva. The works to be included are being identified.

bullinger.name: Heinrich Bullinger
bullinger.desc: Reformer of Zurich. The Decades and other works are under review.

fathers.name: Church Fathers
fathers.desc: Latin and Greek patristic works, beginning with Augustine, are under review.

puritans.name: Puritans
puritans.desc: Since their works were written in English, their translation priority is set separately.

schilder.name: Klaas Schilder
schilder.desc: Dutch Reformed theologian. He taught at the Theological Seminary in Kampen and is known for his works on covenant theology and on the sufferings of Christ.

reformed.name: The Reformed Churches
reformed.desc: Confessions and catechisms publicly adopted by the Reformed churches through their synods and assemblies after the Reformation. These are not the work of a single author but documents the church has confessed together.

geneva.name: Open Geneva Series
geneva.desc: A series translating all 59 volumes of Calvin's collected works (CO) into Korean from the original languages. Each branch has its own volume numbering.

sermons.name: Calvin's Sermons
sermons.note: French sermons, rendered in the formal Korean polite style.

commentaries.name: Calvin's Commentaries
commentaries.note: Latin commentaries, to be translated in order from CO 23–57.

treatises.name: Calvin's Treatises
treatises.note: The Institutes, treatises, catechisms, and confessions (CO 1–9, 22).

reformed.name: Reformed Classics
reformed.desc: Public-domain works of Reformed theologians after Calvin, translated from the original languages.

treatises.name: Doctrine & Treatises
treatises.note: Translated from the original languages in the formal Korean polite style.

creeds.name: Creeds
creeds.desc: Translations of the creeds, confessions, and catechisms the church has confessed, from the original texts in public-domain editions (Schaff, Niemeyer, Müller, Calvin's collected works).

ancient.name: Ancient creeds
ancient.note: Translated from the Latin and Greek originals in Schaff, vol. 2.

three-forms.name: The Three Forms of Unity
three-forms.note: The Belgic Confession (French), the Heidelberg Catechism (German), and the Canons of Dort (Latin), from Schaff, vol. 3.

ecumenical/ancient-creeds.title: The Creeds of the Ancient Church
ecumenical/ancient-creeds.cite_title: The Creeds of the Ancient Church
ecumenical/ancient-creeds.summary: The Apostles' Creed, the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed (Eastern and Western received forms), the Definition of Chalcedon, and the Athanasian Creed, read article by article alongside the Latin and Greek texts in Schaff's edition.
ecumenical/ancient-creeds.source_short: Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, vol. 2 (4th ed., 1919)

volumes.1: The Creeds of the Ancient Church

calvin/co01-institutio.title: Institutes of the Christian Religion, 1536 and 1539–1554 Editions (CO 1)
calvin/co01-institutio.summary: Volume 1 of Calvin's collected works (Institutio religionis christianae), in CO column order: the first edition of the Institutes (Basel, 1536: the dedicatory preface to Francis I and six chapters), and the 1539–1554 edition, which combines the 1539 Strasbourg edition with the additions of the 1543, 1545, 1550, 1553, and 1554 editions (the letter to the reader, the dedicatory preface, and 21 chapters).

calvin/co02-institutio.title: Institutes of the Christian Religion, 1559 Edition (CO 2)
calvin/co02-institutio.summary: Volume 2 of Calvin's collected works (Institutio christianae religionis, 1559). The final Geneva edition of 1559, which Calvin thoroughly revised and rearranged into four books and 80 chapters, in CO column order from the letter to the reader and the dedicatory preface to Francis I through Book 4, Chapter 20, on civil government.

calvin/co08-tractatus.title: Calvin's Treatises (CO 8)
calvin/co08-tractatus.summary: Volume 8 of Calvin's collected works (Tractatus theologici minores 4), in CO column order: On Scandals (1550), the Congregation on Eternal Election (1551), the records of the Bolsec trial, On the Eternal Predestination of God (1552), Four Sermons (1552), the Defense of the Orthodox Faith concerning the Holy Trinity (1554), and thirty letters of Servetus with the records of his trial.

calvin/hezekiah-isaiah-sermons.title: Sermons on the Song of Hezekiah and Isaiah 53
calvin/hezekiah-isaiah-sermons.cite_title: Sermons on the Song of Hezekiah and Isaiah 53
calvin/hezekiah-isaiah-sermons.summary: Four sermons on the Song of Hezekiah (Isaiah 38) and seven sermons on Isaiah 53, with the prefaces to the first editions of both collections.

volumes.4: Sermons on the Song of Hezekiah and Isaiah 53

calvin/job-sermons.title: Sermons on Job
calvin/job-sermons.summary: The 159 sermons Calvin preached through the whole book of Job in Geneva in 1554–1555, first published in Geneva in 1563.

schilder/wat-is-de-hel.title: What Is Hell?
schilder/wat-is-de-hel.summary: The third edition (1932) by Klaas Schilder (1890–1952), based on his 1919 lecture in Vlaardingen and greatly expanded in 1932. It sets out the biblical teaching on hell from the standpoint of Reformed theology and answers objections.

schilder/heidelbergsche-catechismus.title: Commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism
schilder/heidelbergsche-catechismus.summary: Klaas Schilder's (1890–1952) commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism, begun in 1938 and published in four volumes in 1947–1953. It covers Lord's Days 1–10 (Questions 1–28) and remained unfinished at the author's death.

volumes.1: Commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism 1 (Lord's Days 1–4)
volumes.2: Commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism 2 (Lord's Days 5–7)
volumes.3: Commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism 3 (Lord's Days 8–9)
volumes.4: Commentary on the Heidelberg Catechism 4 (Lord's Day 10)

reformed/belgic-confession.title: The Belgic Confession
reformed/belgic-confession.summary: The confession of faith in 37 articles written in French by Guido de Brès in 1561 for the churches of Flanders and the Netherlands and revised by the Synod of Dort in 1619, read article by article alongside the French text in Schaff's edition (the authentic manuscript of 1580 with the Dort revision).
reformed/belgic-confession.source_short: Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3 (4th ed., 1919)

reformed/heidelberg-catechism.title: The Heidelberg Catechism
reformed/heidelberg-catechism.summary: The catechism of 129 questions published at Heidelberg in 1563 by order of Elector Frederick III of the Palatinate, read question by question alongside the German text of 1563 in Schaff's edition.
reformed/heidelberg-catechism.source_short: Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3 (4th ed., 1919)

reformed/canons-of-dort.title: The Canons of Dort
reformed/canons-of-dort.summary: The judgment of the National Synod of Dordrecht (1618–1619) on the five disputed heads of doctrine: the preface, the articles and rejections of errors of each head, and the conclusion, read article by article alongside the official Latin text in Schaff's edition.
reformed/canons-of-dort.source_short: Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3 (4th ed., 1919)

gnv.note: Geneva Bible 1599. A Reformed English Bible produced in Calvin's Geneva. Public domain.

kjv.name: King James Version (KJV)
kjv.note: King James (Authorized) Version. Words in brackets, supplied by the translators, are shown in italics. Public domain.

webp.name: World English Bible
webp.note: World English Bible (66-book edition, LORD form). Public domain. "World English Bible" is a trademark.

bsb.name: Berean Standard Bible
bsb.note: Berean Standard Bible. Dedicated to the public domain on April 30, 2023.
